features.title: Register converted bootc qcow2 as Proxmox VM template (stateless cloud-init)
features.description: Ansible playbook and role register the staged RHEL 10 bootc qcow2 as a Ceph-backed Proxmox VM template with UEFI, q35, virtio-scsi, virtio NIC, cloud-init drive, and stateless cloud-init via a vendor-data snippet. title: Mount CephFS cFS on bootc_targets VMs
description: Ansible role and playbook pull ceph.conf and client.rhel keyring from 1Password, add the CephX key to the Linux kernel keyring, and persistently mount the CephFS filesystem 'cFS' at /mnt/cfs on all bootc_targets VMs.
user_visible_behavior: All three bootc VMs (rhvm-01/02/03) have /mnt/cfs mounted and accessible; ceph-rhel-keyring.service ensures the kernel keyring is populated before local-fs.target at boot.
verification: LIVE: ansible-playbook ansible/playbooks/bootc_ceph_mount.yaml -> ok=14 changed=4 failed=0 on all three VMs
df -h /mnt/cfs shows 6.2T CephFS on all three VMs
evidence: 2026-06-18 LIVE (operator-approved via session continuation): op run --env-file ansible/op-run.ceph.example -- ansible-playbook ansible/playbooks/bootc_ceph_mount.yaml -> PLAY RECAP: rhvm-01/02/03 ok=14 changed=4 failed=0. Mounts verified: 10.10.10.18:6789,...:/ 6.2T 112G 6.1T 2% /var/mnt/cfs on all three VMs. ceph-rhel-keyring.service enabled on all three VMs.

2026-06-18 Root-cause chain resolved: (1) secretfile= rejected — ceph-common not installed so mount.ceph helper absent; (2) kernel 6.12 requires binary-decoded CephX key in Linux kernel keyring before mount — key=<base64> is a keyring DESCRIPTION lookup, not a raw value; (3) fsname= renamed to mds_namespace= in kernel 5.4+; (4) v1/msgr1 mon addresses (port 6789) explicit in src, bypassing ceph.conf msgr2-format parsing issues. Fix: keyctl padd ceph <base64-desc> @s with binary payload, then key=<base64> in mount options. Boot persistence: ceph-rhel-keyring.service (Before=local-fs.target) calls /etc/ceph/load-keyring.py.
2026-06-18 ./init.sh -> static baseline complete.

notes: VMs running bootc .5 image (ceph-common baked in). mount.ceph present but kernel CephFS client handles mount directly. The keyring credential (op://d3HLPRV/ufj6ka4i7gmqwky7i6djulkrgq) contains client.rhel with caps mds='allow rw fsname=cFS' / mon='allow r fsname=cFS' / osd='allow rw tag cephfs data=cFS'.
